To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

teachers' work is commonly and powerfully represented as a conservative practice, that teachers and teacher educators have a tenacious attachment to such representations, and that such attachments have a powerful impact on the ways in which teachers and teacher educators understand and enact their work.
The visual representations of teachers and teaching that we have identified and analysed in this paper, in a wide range of media, are deeply conservative.
teachers' work, and the work of teaching, is represented in ways that are highly conservative and that are problematic in the context of the transformation of teachers' work.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the work the representation(s) of teachers' work do.

the ways in which visual imagery of teachers' work is implicated in the reproduction of conservative representations of teachers' and teachers' work, and the implications of this for our own self representations and practices.

the way in which the visual representations of teachers work that we use to imagine, and represent to others, the work we do, work to constitute a conservative repertoire of meanings that limit our capacity to imagine, and enact, practices that are more progressive and transformative.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the work the representation does is that it works.
this paper is a call to arms for a more radical and reflexive approach to the visual representation of teaching and teachers' work.
this paper is an invitation to think about our own self representation practices, and to consider the ways in which our practices might work to constitute and reproduce conservative practices.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the visual representation of teachers' and teachers' work is a critical resource on which we might draw to transform our practice.
teachers' work is a complex phenomenon that is represented and constituted by a range of discourses and practices that are often in conflict with each other, and with the practices of teachers.
the representation of teachers work is a very complex process that has a strong influence on how we perceive the work and the teachers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we need to be more self critical about our own self representations, and to develop a more reflexive approach to self representations of teaching and teachers' work.
it is important to pay attention to how teachers are represented, and to the work such representations do.
we are not only what we think, but what we think we think.
